summary: Moderate remaining privacy concern in the local Firestore rules: same-household reads expose whole user profiles, including email, notification preferences and messaging tokens. The original seven cross-household, entitlement, role and malformed-data failures are repaired. The expanded Auth/rules emulator suite passes 43/43 checks with positive collaboration, atomic creation, invitation refresh and bounded legacy compatibility. This assesses local code only; production rules were not deployed or audited in this repair pass.

findings.issue: Members can read complete profiles of other members of their household. Firestore does not redact email, fcmToken or notification settings from those reads.
findings.recommendation: Split public household member fields from private per-user settings and device tokens, then restrict private documents to their owner and trusted server operations. Migrate the member query and notification handler together.

findings.issue: Document field sizes and numeric ranges are bounded, but a member can create many lists/items or repeatedly call invitation acceptance. Rules do not provide request-rate or aggregate storage limits.
findings.recommendation: Add appropriate App Check enforcement, backend rate limiting and usage monitoring before broad distribution.

findings.issue: Updates may retain an existing bounded nonblank quantity label or an exactly unchanged blank display name for legacy compatibility. New and changed values are strictly validated. Legacy items without householdId are absent from group queries.
findings.recommendation: Plan a trusted migration of legacy profiles/items, with a reviewed quantity conversion policy; then remove compatibility allowances when no longer needed.
